selected.rationale: HomeTimelineService fans out per-post reads to post-storage; injected delay is multiplied by timeline length, producing unbounded latency amplification and likely tripping downstream timeouts.
Loss on the fan-out post-storage read has no retry or fallback, so a single dropped response can fail the whole home-timeline read and the probability of failure grows with timeline length.

ComposePost synchronously waits on the home-timeline write, a secondary side-effect; losing this call aborts post creation and exposes an architecture-level coupling defect with no deferred/async write.
Post-storage is the persistence core of compose-post; loss on this critical edge without retry means the post is not stored and the primary write API fails after the timeout.
Unique-id is an early idempotent dependency; a lost response is not retried, so ComposePost cannot generate a post ID and the entire compose request fails.
Text is a mandatory post-content dependency; losing this call without retry blocks every text-bearing post and makes the compose API fail, revealing missing retry defense on the core path.
The user-timeline write is a required side effect for the author's own timeline; loss without retry causes the compose operation to fail or the post to disappear from the user timeline.
Post-storage is a shared dependency for both compose-post and home-timeline; killing it takes down multiple business paths until restart, exposing single-point-of-failure and recovery behavior.
